A 66-year-old male patient seeks medical attention for episodes of retrosternal pain and dyspnea
occurring over the past 10 days. These symptoms manifest during stair climbing or brisk treadmill
walking and subside with rest. The previous night, he experienced dizziness and weakness during one
such episode. He reports having had a cold 2 weeks prior. His medical history includes type 2 diabetes
mellitus diagnosed 4 years ago, managed with glyburide. Physical examination reveals a
well-appearing patient with a weak pulse of 89/min, respiratory rate of 17/min, and blood pressure of
144/85 mm Hg. A late systolic ejection murmur is detected at the second right intercostal space during
cardiovascular examination. Lung auscultation is normal. What is the most likely pathophysiologic
mechanism causing this patient's clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Microvascular dysfunction
(B) Impaired diastolic relaxation (C) Increased left ventricular oxygen demand (D) Left ventricular
outflow tract obstruction (E) Narrowing of the coronary arterial lumen (F) Endothelial dysfunction due to
diabetes (G) Decreased coronary perfusion pressure (H) Coronary artery vasospasm (I) Autonomic
dysfunction affecting coronary blood flow (J) Lymphocytic infiltration of the myocardium
 A. Autonomic dysfunction affecting coronary blood flow
B. Narrowing of the coronary arterial lumen
C. Microvascular dysfunction
D. Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
E. Endothelial dysfunction due to diabetes
F. Decreased coronary perfusion pressure
G. Coronary artery vasospasm
H. Lymphocytic infiltration of the myocardium
I. Increased left ventricular oxygen demand
J. Impaired diastolic relaxation
